motivation: Tajima's 1979 proposal (with the late John Dawson) that an intense laser pulse drives a plasma wake whose fields exceed conventional accelerator gradients by three orders of magnitude founded a new field. Malka and colleagues demonstrated quasi-monoenergetic, high-quality electron beams from laser wakefields (2004), and pioneered their control and applications. Leemans pushed the concept to GeV-scale energies with guided, capillary-discharge wakes (2006, and 8 GeV in 2019), turning a scientific curiosity into a credible accelerator technology. Laser wakefield accelerators now drive compact betatron and Compton X-ray and gamma sources, free-electron-laser demonstrations, and the first experiments probing radiation reaction and strong-field QED in laser-electron collisions. These are physical regimes previously inaccessible in laboratories. This is a fundamental discovery in plasma physics that opened a new experimental frontier, following naturally on the 2018 prize for chirped pulse amplification.
